title: Engineering AI Systems and Agents
prereq_raw: 6.3900 AND (6.1020 OR 6.1800 OR 6.1810); or permission of instructor. Recommended: 6.1210.
description: Introduces principles, abstractions, algorithms, and processes for building, evaluating, and optimizing stochastic AI software systems that invoke pre-trained foundation models inside computer programs. Topics include programming models for language model systems; structured generation and constrained decoding; evaluation, robustness, and security of agentic AI applications; neural information retrieval and retrieval-augmented generation; tool use and agent harnesses; adaptation of model behavior through prompt optimization, supervised fine-tuning, synthetic data, reinforcement learning, and distillation; and serving and runtime systems for language model applications. Includes a substantial project.

title: Introduction to LLM Inference Systems
prereq_raw: 6.1800 (Computer Systems Engineering) or equivalent systems background; parallel/performance programming (e.g. 6.1060) recommended.
description: Examines large language model (LLM) inference as a systems problem, with emphasis on low-latency execution, memory-intensive workloads, and deployment across heterogeneous hardware. Topics include batching and scheduling, KV-cache management, kernel and compiler co-design, distributed and multi-GPU inference, and hardware tradeoffs across GPUs, CPUs, TPUs, and inference accelerators. Also covers inference-time optimization such as quantization, sparsity, speculative decoding, and multi-model routing. Emphasizes analytical understanding and synthesis of recent research and production systems rather than large programming projects.

title: AI for Science: Generative AI for Scientific Discovery
prereq_raw: Machine learning (6.3900/6.7900/6.C51+6.C511 or related); probability (6.3700/6.3800 or related); linear algebra (18.06/6.C06 or related).
description: Project-based course on emerging opportunities of generative AI in scientific research. Draws on recent literature on representation and grounding of scientific knowledge, generative approaches, inverse design, closed-loop discovery, and agentic approaches to scientific discovery. Students critically review papers, participate in structured discussion, and complete a substantial class project involving generative AI. Emphasizes technical understanding, rigorous evaluation, and potential for scientific advances. Enrollment may be limited.

title: Audio Computing: Processing Sound in Engineering, Science, and the Arts
prereq_raw: Familiarity with programming, and basic calculus.
description: Covers an extensive range of topics relating to sound and vibration analysis, focusing on computational tools to process such data, with applications across disciplines. Material includes basic signal processing, vibration and acoustical simulations and measurements, machine-learning audio, microphone and speaker arrays, signal enhancement and restoration, and psychoacoustics. Applications include 3D audio, sound-event classifiers, basic speech recognition, auto-tuners and music production tools, audio compression, modeling of voice/instruments/rooms, real-time audio, and source separation. (Cross-listed 21M; AAGS in Signals & Systems. Grad version has additional assignments.)

title: Topics in Error-Correcting Codes for Computer Science
description: Introduces the theory of error-correcting codes to computer scientists, focusing on results of asymptotic or algorithmic significance. Principal topics: existence results for error-correcting codes and limitations; constructions and algorithms; interactive coding; and applications in computer science.

title: Quantum Error Correction
description: Develops the theory and practice of quantum error correction (QEC) and fault-tolerant quantum computation, with emphasis on recent developments. Covers stabilizer codes, the Knill-Laflamme conditions, the fault-tolerance stack with surface codes (lattice surgery, transversal gates, non-Clifford gates, decoding), high-rate quantum LDPC codes, logical gate design, and end-to-end fault-tolerant architecture design with resource estimation. Students simulate and benchmark QEC circuits and complete a research-style final project.
